Hi Soojin,

Primary asks:
- A recommended commit amount to reduce costs while keeping headroom for peaks.
- Timing/approach for migration (can we phase over 4-8 weeks?).
- Any constraints on migration windows and expected downtime.

Attaching: brightpath_nov_usage.csv (usage by hour).

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-11-22T14:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Convert burst capacity to committed pool — BrightPath

Thanks for the data and the call earlier. I pulled a quick telemetry snapshot (attached) and here are my observations and recommendation.

Telemetry highlights:
- Historical committed: 80 GPUs.
- Observed 30-day median sustained usage: ~75 GPUs.
- 95th percentile sustained windows (1h rolling): 110 GPUs.
- Peak bursts (multi-hour): up to 140 GPUs, typically during batch jobs and nightly retrain scoring.
- Average utilization on active instances: ~62% (this is at token-generation steady-state; KV cache reuse reduces per-token cost but not peak slot needs).

Recommendation: phased right-shift to steady-state commit of 120 GPUs with a 10% operational buffer (target 132 effective slots) on a 12-month term. Phase plan:
- Phase A (30 days): commit 100 GPUs to validate load shaping and adjust autoscale thresholds.
- Phase B (60 days): increase to 120 GPUs once observed 30-day steady metrics match projections.
- Fallback: maintain 40-GPU burst pool for rare peaks while monitoring latency SLAs.

Rationale: 120 GPUs aligns with 95th percentile sustained needs while keeping a small burst pool to handle spikes without SLA impact. Thermal/placement note: some of BrightPath's heavy batch windows will need cross-rack placement; we'll coordinate with infra to avoid noisy-neighborctions.

Attaching: telemetry_snapshot.pdf

-Karthik
Senior Infra Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@brightpath.ai>, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-24T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Convert burst capacity to committed pool — BrightPath

Elaine — attaching an initial commercial sketch and SOW that maps to Karthik's operational plan. Key commercial points below (draft):

- Proposed committed baseline: 120 GPUs (12-month term).
- Intro tranche: 100 GPUs for first 30 days at commit pricing to validate metrics; if validated, tranche converts to full 120 for remainder of term.
- Pricing: tiered per-GPU pricing, with a stepdown at 150+ (not expected in steady-state).
- Credits: one-time migration credit to offset orchestration cost (applied in month 1).
- SLA: standard Dedicated SLAs apply; will include a clause for emergency burst headroom for up to 40 GPUs.

Next steps requested from BrightPath:
1) Procurement signoff on commercial terms + any required PO cadence.
2) Confirmation of preferred migration windows (we recommend weekend low-traffic windows for Phase A).

Attachments: SOW-BrightPath-draft.pdf
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8342

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Can you confirm expected migration downtime or user impact for Phase A? Our ops team needs a firm SLA on latency during the tranche conversion.
- Will the initial 100 -> 120 ramp require model restarts or KV cache invalidations? Any guidance we should prepare for on our side?

Procurement: we'll need an itemized invoice and the SOW redline for PO processing.

Ops (cc): please advise on acceptable maintenance windows; we prefer Saturday 02:00-06:00 PT.

Regards,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform, BrightPath AI
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Cc: ops@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: Convert burst capacity to committed pool — BrightPath

Elaine — great, thanks for the quick turn. To answer your questions and keep momentum:

- Migration impact: Phase A is designed to be non-disruptive. We will perform a live reallocation of capacity with rolling placements; customers should see brief connection rebalances (~15-45s) on a small subset of in-flight requests during placement windows. No application downtime expected.
- Model/KV behavior: model processes will not require full restarts; KV cache warming is expected — Karthik's team will pre-warm caches for critical routes. We recommend scheduling heavy batch jobs outside the initial 48-hour validation window.
- Ops window: Saturday 02:00-06:00 PT is acceptable for Phase A start. We'll coordinate a 4-hour maintenance window and provide a rollback playbook.

Action items (mutual action plan):
- BrightPath: sign SOW redline + provide PO (procurement).
- Redwood (Ben): finalize SOW and send DocuSign link.
- Redwood (Karthik): schedule Phase A placement and share runbook with ops@brightpath.ai.
- Both: 30-day telemetry check-in meeting (T+30) to validate commit.

I'll send the DocuSign link once Ben uploads the final SOW. Forwarding earlier summaries below for context.
